#### List:

- Air
- Blood
- Homeostasis
- Drugs

#### Air:

+----------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Reservoir      | - For gas exchange during expiration, between breaths, during apnoea (e.g.heavy lifting) |
+----------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Humidification | - Countercurrent heat and moisture exchange                                              |
|                | - Purpose                                                                                |
|                |   - Prevent heat loss                                                                    |
|                |   - Prevent water loss                                                                   |
|                |   - Prevent crusting of secretions                                                       |
|                |   - Maintain mucociliary function                                                        |
|                |   - Prevent infection                                                                    |
|                | - Mechanism                                                                              |
|                |   - Cool dry air inhaled                                                                 |
|                |     - ↑Temp by conduction, convection                                                    |
|                |     - Evaporation→ humidification due to ↓ relative humidity                             |
|                |   - Warm, humidified air exhaled                                                         |
|                |     - ↓Temp by conduction, convection                                                    |
|                |     - Condensation→drying due to ↑ relative humidity                                     |
+----------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Filtration     | - Particles e.g. dust, pathogens e.g. viruses, bacteria                                  |
|                | - \>3um: stick to airway → mucociliary escalator → swallowed                             |
|                | - 1-3um: sediment in alveoli → phagocytosis by macrophage = dust cell                    |
|                | - \<1um free in air ± deposit anywhere                                                   |
+----------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Immune         | - Innate: mucociliary escalator, lysozyme, macrophage                                    |
|                | - Adaptive: IgA, IgG in alveolar lining fluid                                            |
+----------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Phonation      | - Exhalation against variably closed glottis                                             |
+----------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

#### Blood:

+------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Pump       | - Inspiration: ↓ intrathoracic pressure → ↑ gradient for systemic venous return |
|            | - Expiration: venous valves prevent flow reversal                               |
|            | - Cardiac output higher during spontaneous ventilation than during apnoea       |
+------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Reservoir  | - 15% blood volume supine (8% arteries, 3% capillaries, 5% veins)               |
|            | - 9% blood volume erect                                                         |
+------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Filtration | - Of microemboli to prevent stroke                                              |
+------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

#### Homeostasis:

+-----------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Acid-base | - CO~2~ excretion for homeostasis                                            |
|           |   - 15,000mmol/day by Krebs cycle in mitochondria during aerobic respiration |
|           |   - Alveolar ventilation is coupled to metabolic rate via control of PaCO~2~ |
|           | - CO~2~ excretion for compensation during metabolic acidosis                 |
|           |   - CO~2~ + H~2~O \<-\> H^+^ + HCO~3~^-^                                     |
|           |   - ↑Alveolar ventilation → left shift → ↑pH                                 |
+-----------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Fluid     | - Endothelial angiotensin-converting enzyme: AT1 (inactive) → AT2 (active)   |
|           | - AT2: Na^+^/H~2~O reabsorption, vasoconstriction                            |
+-----------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Metabolic | - Inactivate serotonin near 100%, bradykinin 80%, noradrenaline 30%          |
|           | - Inactivate PGE~2~, PGF~2~~α~, leukotrienes                                 |
+-----------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

#### Drugs:

+------------+------------------------------------------------+
| Route      | - Local: e.g. salbutamol                       |
|            | - Systemic: e.g. naloxone                      |
+------------+------------------------------------------------+
| Reservoir  | - e.g. first pass uptake of fentanyl up to 75% |
+------------+------------------------------------------------+
| Metabolism | - e.g. ? propofol and CYP450                   |
+------------+------------------------------------------------+
| Excretion  | - e.g. sevoflurane                             |
+------------+------------------------------------------------+
